blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.recommendation: Flatten and name the rules so the function reads without the plan. Skip rows with an empty email by an early `continue` (`if row.email.is_empty() { continue; }`) and say in a comment why such rows are dropped. Extract the duplicated seat loop (lines 19-26 and 31-36) into one helper, e.g. `add_new_seats(db, account_id, existing, seats) -> Result<usize, DbError>`, whose filters use `Iterator::filter` and a named predicate such as `is_seat_email(seat)` instead of the bare `seat.contains('@')`, so the reader learns that a seat is an email address and that others are skipped. Replace the nested `if !account.seats.contains(seat)` / `if seat.contains('@')` pair with one combined condition. The condition `if account.plan != row.plan` is the line a newcomer would misread: nothing says why seats are only added to an existing account whose plan differs from the CSV row (and the plan itself is never updated); the proposal only says "creates missing accounts and their seats". Name that rule with a comment or a well-named function stating why, so the reader does not take it for a bug or a typo for `==`. This restructuring must keep the current behaviour.
findings.title: `import` nests six levels deep, duplicates its seat loop and leaves its filters unexplained
